A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Model Extrapolation Expedites Alignment and contain 17 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the complete text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original controlled DPO experiments, evaluations of EXPO on existing aligned LLMs, ablations, and downstream-task results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Sections 3–4 and Appendix D, including comparisons between original and extrapolated models.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same EXPO procedure, θ2 = θ1 + α(θ1 − θ0), using an aligned model and its initial SFT checkpoint. No algorithm component, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both retain UltraFeedback, AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench, and the same six downstream benchmarks in Appendix D. The training-data variants and failure-case scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: the same SFT/DPO controls, twelve aligned LLMs in Table 5, and seven alignment algorithms in Table 6 are evaluated with and without EXPO.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains the 61K/1K UltraFeedback split, 805-instruction AlpacaEval evaluation, training configurations, decoding settings, and metrics. The experimental protocols in Section 4 and the appendices also match.

E4.justification: Both contain the same interpolation check, reward-distribution and α analyses, training-data and configuration ablations, failure cases in Section 4.3, and alignment-tax analysis in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Section 3.1 specifies sampling seed 42 in both versions. No repeated-run information, uncertainty-reporting practice, or statistical testing is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results match, including Appendix D. For example, Table 2 retains a 21.3% length-controlled win rate for the 20%-step DPO model with EXPO and 17.3% for the fully trained DPO baseline.

T1.justification: The assumptions and first-order derivation in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Minor norm typesetting and the wording change introducing the implication of Equation 3 do not alter mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient alignment through extrapolation, the 20%-step DPO result, and improvements across 1.8B–70B LLMs. No core contribution is broadened or narrowed.

C2.justification: The explanations involving length bias, parameter-change magnitude, and overfitting are retained. Sections 4.3 and 6 preserve the same failure conditions, manual hyperparameter-search limitation, and alignment-tax tradeoff.

D1.justification: Training and inference details, hardware and computational-cost estimates, Appendix B search instructions, Appendix C model IDs, and code/model access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, Appendix A related-work discussion, and Section 2.3 positioning relative to model averaging/interpolation are unchanged. Bibliography entries move with the reference reflow but are not added or removed.

P1.justification: v4 adds an Acknowledgements section recognizing contributors, reviewers, and funding. It changes 'From Equation 3' to 'According to Equation 3' in Section 2.3 and updates the arXiv version/date; the scientific narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements reflow the references across pages 10–13, alongside small mathematical typesetting and line-wrapping changes elsewhere. Figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 makes contributor and funding attribution more complete, while retaining the same scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations. The acknowledgements and small wording/layout edits do not establish a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
